men tightening flanged handles 9.5-19 mm wide (Imrhan and Munoz-Vasa 2013): at 19 mm mean 0.77 N·m, 95th percentile 0.95; carried on to 34.5 mm (beyond the data: an extrapolation) mean 1.17, 95th percentile 1.36; Swain et al. (1970) 1.06
taken here: 1.36 N·m, the largest (a strong hand, forcing it on the wide paddle); wempe_strength.js sizes the stop for Swain's 1.06

Wound forward against the stop (full wind): the stop takes the key's torque less the chain's (0.355 N·m measured, 05 06_20 at 262 mm; 0.397 frictionless: the smaller taken off). wempe_strength.js adds them (its stop lines are the larger)

the wire's end turned down into the body's hole: bent through a right angle there, it is the place the coil would give first; a maker forms it on a radius, not sharp
